plan.title: Warm-Wood Entry Bench with Lower Shelf
plan.summary: Build the foreground bench in the photo: a solid-pine seat, straight square legs, discreet aprons and a lower storage shelf. Glued dowels and corner blocks stiffen the frame; movement-friendly fasteners secure the solid-wood seat and shelf.
assumptions: The intended project is the foreground bench, not the larger dining table behind it.
Dimensions are estimated from the photograph; the proposed bench is 1200 mm wide, 400 mm deep and 450 mm high.
Select pine with a warm brown finish approximates the photograph economically; the photographed wood species and hidden joints cannot be identified.
Use straight, dry, knot-free stock at all joints and commercially edge-glued solid-pine panels for the seat and shelf.
Seat and shelf grain runs left to right. Figure-eight fasteners allow their front-to-back seasonal movement.
The design is intended for ordinary seated use by one adult and up to 15 kg of evenly distributed shelf storage. It is not a certified load-rated product or a standing platform.
Upper apron ends use two 8 mm dowels each, reinforced by four corner blocks. Lower rail ends also use two 8 mm dowels each.
Figure-eight fastener dimensions vary. Select approximately 30 mm long fasteners supplied with screws suitable for 30 mm panels, and verify their required shallow recess before cutting it.
clarifying_questions: Do you want the foreground bench, as assumed here, or the larger table behind it?
Should the bench accommodate more than one adult at a time?

steps.title: Cut and identify the parts
steps.text: Cut P1 (seat), P2 (legs), P3 (long aprons), P4 (upper side aprons), P5 (lower rails) and P6 (shelf) to the listed dimensions. Cut P7–P10 (corner blocks) to their mirrored plan-view profiles from 30 mm stock. Label inside faces and each leg location, and check that all four legs are exactly the same length.
tools_used: Tape measure, square and marking pencil
Saw with straightedge and angle guide
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection for powered cutting. Clamp small block blanks to a larger carrier or cut them by hand; never hold tiny pieces beside a moving blade.
steps.tip: Cut the four legs against the same stop setting rather than measuring them separately.

steps.title: Drill dowel holes and recess the tabletop hardware
steps.text: Use the doweling jig to drill two 8 mm holes in every P3, P4 and P5 end and transfer their exact positions to P2 (legs), following the heights in the part notes. Bore approximately 31 mm deep on each side for 60 mm dowels and glue relief. Make shallow figure-eight fastener recesses in the top edges of P3, P4 and P5 at the joint-note locations, using the actual hardware as a template.
tools_used: Tape measure, square and marking pencil
Drill/driver with 8 mm brad-point bit, pilot bits, clearance bit and countersink
Self-centering doweling jig and depth stops
steps.safety: Clamp every workpiece before drilling or chiseling, wear eye protection, and keep both hands behind the chisel edge.
steps.tip: The long-apron and side-apron dowels deliberately use different heights so their holes do not cross inside the legs.

steps.title: Dry-fit and pre-sand
steps.text: Dry-fit P2–P5 with dowels but without glue, checking the 330 mm upper-apron bottom height and 145 mm lower-rail top height. Confirm that the frame is square, its top edges are flush, and P7–P10 fit against both adjacent aprons, with each clipped edge just meeting its leg's inner vertical corner without forcing it. Disassemble and sand all parts through 120 and 180 grit, leaving glue surfaces clean and unrounded.
tools_used: Tape measure, square and marking pencil
Long bar clamps and smaller clamps
steps.safety: Wear a dust respirator and use extraction when power-sanding. Handle dry-fit assemblies gently because unglued joints can separate.
steps.tip: Ease the seat's exposed edges enough to remove sharpness, but keep the underside bearing surfaces flat.

steps.title: Glue the doweled frame
steps.text: First assemble the two side frames from P2 (legs), P4 (upper side aprons) and P5 (lower rails), using two 8 x 60 mm fluted dowels at each of their eight joints. After those subassemblies set, join them with both P3 (long aprons), using two more 8 x 60 mm dowels at each of four ends; the frame uses 24 dowels total. Apply glue to mating faces and hole walls, clamp square for at least 60 minutes per glue-up or the adhesive's stated minimum, and leave the completed frame overnight before stressing it.
tools_used: Long bar clamps and smaller clamps
Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.safety: Support both side frames during the long-apron glue-up so they cannot fall or trap fingers.
steps.tip: Compare the frame's diagonals before the glue grabs; equal diagonals indicate a square assembly.

steps.title: Reinforce the four upper corners
steps.text: Glue P7–P10 (corner blocks) against both adjacent apron faces with their bottoms at 360 mm above the floor. Position each clipped edge just against the corresponding P2 (leg) inner corner as a dry line contact, with no glue or fastener between block and leg; the apron connections provide the reinforcement. Clamp each block, drill clearance holes through the aprons and pilot holes into the block, then drive two 4 x 40 mm countersunk wood screws per block from the outside apron faces: eight screws total. Use the exact drive locations in J4–J11, keep heads flush, and leave clamps on for at least 60 minutes or the glue manufacturer's minimum.
tools_used: Drill/driver with 8 mm brad-point bit, pilot bits, clearance bit and countersink
Long bar clamps and smaller clamps
Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and keep hands clear of the pilot-bit exit path.
steps.tip: Do not move these screws closer to the diagonal block edge; the specified positions preserve wood around their tips.

steps.title: Install the lower shelf
steps.text: Install two figure-eight fastener kits on each P5 (lower rail), four kits total, using their included screws and no glue. Slide P6 (shelf) lengthwise through a side opening above the lower rails, then lower it onto them with 5 mm clearance at the front and rear. With a helper, rest the frame on a padded side and drive the kits' included shelf screws upward into predrilled holes; use panel screws no longer than 16 mm and leave the fasteners free to pivot.
tools_used: Drill/driver with 8 mm brad-point bit, pilot bits, clearance bit and countersink
Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.safety: Support the shelf while tipping the frame, protect fingers at the rails, and wear eye protection when drilling.
steps.tip: Working with the frame on its side gives straight screwdriver access that the low shelf would otherwise obstruct.

steps.title: Attach the seat without restricting wood movement
steps.text: Fit two figure-eight kits to each P3 (long apron) and one to each P4 (side apron), six kits total, using the included screws and no glue. Lay P1 (seat) face down on clean padding and position the inverted frame with 30 mm clearance from each seat edge to the corresponding outer leg face. Check that all leg tops and upper apron edges bear against the seat, then pilot-drill and install the included seat screws from the open underside, using screws no longer than 16 mm.
tools_used: Tape measure, square and marking pencil
Drill/driver with 8 mm brad-point bit, pilot bits, clearance bit and countersink
steps.safety: Use a helper to invert and position the frame. Set a drill depth stop so pilot holes cannot emerge through the seat.
steps.tip: Do not add glue or rigid screws between the legs and seat; the figure-eight fittings must accommodate seasonal movement.

steps.title: Prepare the assembled bench for finishing
steps.text: Check all joints, remove dried glue carefully, and fill the eight corner-block screw recesses if desired. Sand any handled or filled areas back through 180 grit and vacuum the entire bench. Test the conditioner, brown stain and clear coat together on a matching offcut before applying them to the furniture.
steps.safety: Use dust extraction and a dust respirator for sanding. Ventilate the finishing area and follow each product's protective-equipment instructions.
steps.tip: Glue residue shows up as pale patches under stain; inspect especially around the leg joints.

steps.title: Apply the warm brown color
steps.text: Apply compatible water-based conditioner and stain to the seat, shelf and frame, including hidden faces. Follow the products' application windows and wipe off excess stain evenly with the grain. Allow the stain to dry for the label's stated period, typically at least 4–6 hours, before clear coating.
steps.safety: Wear gloves, maintain ventilation and keep finishing products away from ignition sources. Dispose of used cloths according to the product labels and local rules.
steps.tip: Several light color applications are easier to control on pine than one heavy application.

steps.title: Protect the wood with satin clear coat
steps.text: Apply three thin coats of compatible satin water-based furniture clear coat to exposed surfaces and at least two coats to hidden faces and edges. Allow the label's recoat time, commonly 2–4 hours, and lightly sand between coats only as directed. Keep finish out of the figure-eight pivots and allow full cure before normal use, commonly about 7 days.
steps.safety: Maintain ventilation and wear the protection specified on the finish label. Wear a dust respirator when sanding cured finish.
steps.tip: Dry-to-touch is not the same as fully cured; blankets can imprint a finish that has not hardened.

steps.title: Check stability before use
steps.text: Place the cured bench upright on a level floor and check for rocking, loose hardware or movement at any glued joint. Apply seated load gradually and stop immediately if a joint opens, creaks persistently or shifts; this check is not a certified proof test. Store only light items on P6 (shelf), never stand on either panel, and recheck the fittings after the first month.
steps.safety: Use a helper to turn the finished bench upright. Do not jump on the seat or use the shelf as a step.
steps.tip: Tighten loose hardware gently without locking the figure-eight fittings against seasonal movement.

safety_overview: Wear eye protection when cutting or drilling, hearing protection for powered saws, and a dust respirator when sanding.
Clamp stock securely, especially the small corner blocks; keep hands away from blades and drill exit paths.
Use straight, knot-free structural stock and accurate dowel alignment; reject split legs or damaged joints.
Use a helper when turning the assembled bench, and provide padding and stable support.
Ventilate during finishing, follow product labels, and allow full cure before seating or placing textiles on the bench.
This low bench does not ordinarily need tall-furniture anti-tip hardware; it must not be used for climbing, standing or overhead storage.

review.summary: The bench is buildable as written for the stated one-adult use and light shelf storage. The doweled frame, corner reinforcement, assembly sequence and movement-friendly panel attachments are appropriate. Tool access is workable, including with the shelf installed. One minor finishing-sequence improvement is recommended.

issues.problem: Steps 9–10 call for finishing hidden faces after both panels are attached. The seat-to-frame and shelf-to-rail bearing surfaces are then inaccessible, and applying finish around the installed figure-eight fittings makes it harder to keep their pivots clean.
issues.fix: After the dry fit, finish both faces and all edges of P1 and P6 separately. Finish the glued frame after step 5, keeping finish out of hardware recesses and pilot holes. Allow the finish to cure before installing the panels in steps 6–7; revise steps 8–10 to describe this sequence.

plan.title: Rustic Shed-Roof Bird Nest Box
plan.summary: An untreated cedar nest box inspired by the photograph, with a sloping roof, round entrance, rough interior climbing surface, ventilation gaps and a removable floor. The proposed 50 mm entrance is provisional: confirm the intended bird species before drilling it.
assumptions: The photograph shows a rustic wooden nest box with a single sloping roof; dimensions and concealed joints cannot be measured reliably from it.
The estimated body is 220 mm wide and 240 mm deep. This is a medium-sized nest box, not a species-certified nesting design.
Use untreated cedar of actual 19 mm thickness for the walls and roof, and exterior-bond plywood for the removable floor. Do not use pressure-treated wood.

The roof slopes upward toward the back at approximately 16.26 degrees. Its angled board is represented by a rectangular axis placement, with the 240 mm cross-section dimension running horizontally across the box.

Fractional roof coordinates and overall dimensions are calculated drawing coordinates, not measurements to lay out individually. Cut the roof to 300 x 240 x 19 mm and fit it directly against the sloping side tops.
The roof is a purchased edge-glued cedar panel or a single sufficiently wide cedar board; its grain runs along the 300 mm slope length.
The tree is external to the modeled assembly. SITE_TREE in the mounting joint denotes a suitable living tree, not a supplied wooden part.
Exterior glue is used on permanent wall joints only. The floor is removable, and the roof attachment accommodates seasonal movement.
The weathered gray appearance is achieved naturally; do not apply stain, paint, preservative or finish inside the box.
clarifying_questions: Which bird species and geographic region is this nest box intended for?
Will you mount it on a tree or on a post, and can it be reached safely for annual cleaning?

parts.name: Sloping side walls
parts.notes: Cut each side from a 490 x 240 mm blank. The front edge is 420 mm tall and the rear edge is 490 mm tall. Grain runs vertically. Ease sharp edges but leave the interior rough.

parts.name: Entrance wall
parts.notes: Provisional entrance diameter 50 mm, centered 91 mm from either side and 300 mm above the wall bottom. Confirm species requirements before drilling. The top is intentionally below the roof for ventilation. Do not add a perch.

parts.name: Rear wall
parts.notes: Leave the small roof gap open for ventilation. Mounting holes are drilled during installation preparation, clear of wall-joint dowels.

parts.name: Removable drainage floor
parts.notes: Four 8 mm drainage holes. Floor withdraws downward after its four retaining screws are removed. It is a snug sliding fit, not a glued panel.

parts.name: Sloping roof
parts.notes: The 240 mm cross-section dimension runs along world x. Centerline rise is 84 mm and run is 288 mm, giving exactly 300 mm length. Fit its underside flush to both side slopes. Keep the square-cut front and rear ends; the calculated bounding dimensions include their thickness projection.

joints.note: Exterior glue on mating edges and dowels. Drill 15 mm into each member. Dowel centers are 65, 200 and 360 mm above the bottom.

joints.drive_from: Drill the side-wall inside faces and rear-wall mating edges before assembly; press together with clamps.
joints.note: Exterior glue on mating edges and dowels. Drill 15 mm into each member. Dowel centers are 65, 230 and 420 mm above the bottom.

joints.drive_from: Offer the floor upward from underneath during the fit inspection.
joints.note: Unfastened, unglued edge contact in the fixed geometry. IMPORTANT UNRESOLVED CONSTRAINT: P4 exactly fills the nominal opening, leaving no seasonal clearance. Approximately 2 mm clearance at every floor edge requires changing P4 from 202 x 182 mm to 198 x 178 mm and changing its placement. That modification is not authorized in this joints-and-steps-only repair. Do not install the floor or place the box outdoors until the part geometry is corrected.

joints.drive_from: From the exterior entrance-wall face through counterbored clearance holes into the plywood floor edge.
joints.note: Conditional on an authorized floor-clearance correction; no glue. Locate holes from the fitted floor. With a 2 mm front clearance, a 7 mm deep counterbore leaves 12 mm of cedar and 2 mm of clearance ahead of 16 mm screw embedment in plywood. Locate screw centers at the floor's mid-thickness and approximately 40 mm from each entrance-wall side edge.

joints.drive_from: From the exterior rear-wall face before mounting, through counterbored clearance holes into the plywood floor edge.
joints.note: Conditional on an authorized floor-clearance correction; no glue. Locate holes from the fitted floor. With a 2 mm rear clearance, a 7 mm deep counterbore leaves 12 mm cedar and 2 mm clearance ahead of 16 mm plywood embedment. Remove the box from its mount before releasing the rear screws for cleaning.

fasteners.name: Stainless steel slotted angle bracket
fasteners.size: 30 x 30 x 25 mm, 2 mm thick, 90 degrees; 5 x 12 mm transverse slot in roof flange

joints.drive_from: First through each bracket's side flange into P1's inside broad face with the walls unassembled; subsequently upward through its roof-flange slot into P5's underside, perpendicular to the roof, before fitting the floor.
joints.note: Four brackets, two per side, centered approximately 70 and 170 mm behind the body front. No glue. Each bracket gets one side screw and one roof screw, with a washer under the roof screw. Brackets replace the suggested wooden cleats because adding wooden parts is prohibited. Rotate each bracket along the side slope: its side flange remains against the vertical side face and its roof flange lies parallel to the roof underside. The roof-flange slot must run across the roof grain, along world x. A 16 mm screw through 2 mm steel embeds at most 14 mm, leaving at least 5 mm wood beyond its tip; the roof washer further reduces embedment slightly. Use brackets with countersink-free holes and a supplier working-load rating of at least 50 N per bracket for this attachment. No roof penetrations or exterior sealing washers are required. Side-to-roof bearing contact is included in this joint.

fasteners.name: Tree-friendly nest-box mounting cradle kit
fasteners.size: Rated at least 15 kg; rear-and-side attachment for a 220 mm wide wooden box with 19 mm walls; two wide adjustable tree straps and all attachment hardware included

joints.drive_from: Attach the cradle to the rear wall and both side-wall broad faces according to the kit instructions while the roof and floor are absent.
joints.note: This joint represents the cradle connecting P3 to both copies of P1; the tree is not a part identifier. Select a kit explicitly suitable for these wall thicknesses, with no exposed interior sharp ends and no floor obstruction. Use only its included attachment hardware. Secure the straps to the tree during installation; inspect and loosen them as the tree grows. If no matching kit is available, stop and redesign the mounting rather than substitute unsupported hardware.

joints.drive_from: Lower the roof onto the side-wall slopes from above.
joints.note: Incidental rear-top bearing or near-contact in the fixed geometry, not a primary attachment. Do not glue or fasten the roof to the rear-wall end grain. J6 restrains roof uplift. Preserve the available ventilation opening.

steps.title: Confirm species and resolve the fixed-floor conflict
steps.text: Confirm the intended species before drilling the entrance. The requested seasonal floor clearance cannot be achieved with the fixed 202 x 182 mm P4 and the fixed enclosure geometry. Obtain authorization to revise P4 to 198 x 178 mm, centered with approximately 2 mm clearance at every edge, before continuing to final assembly. The following floor-installation instructions are conditional on that separate geometry correction; they do not authorize changing the supplied parts.
steps.tip: Do not treat a dry-weather sliding fit as evidence that a zero-clearance outdoor floor will remain removable.

steps.title: Prepare the fixed wall and roof blanks
steps.text: Cut P1, P2, P3 and P5 to their listed dimensions, using a guided handsaw instead of a circular saw if preferred. Cut both P1 slopes identically, from 420 mm at the front to 490 mm at the rear; keep the roof ends square. Dry-fit the walls and measure the floor opening, but do not trim P4 under this repair or accept its present zero-clearance fit. Reserve approximately 2 mm clearance at every floor edge for the separately authorized correction.
steps.safety: Clamp stock securely; wear eye, hearing and dust protection with the saw. Keep hands clear of the blade path.
steps.tip: A wood-cleat revision would require additional modeled parts; the roof repair instead uses purchased metal brackets.

steps.title: Prepare the entrance and nesting surfaces
steps.text: Drill P2's species-appropriate entrance, provisionally 50 mm diameter centered 300 mm above the bottom and 91 mm from either side. Drill the four specified 8 mm drainage holes in P4 only after its final geometry has been authorized. Roughen the inside climbing surface beneath the entrance with a rasp and remove loose splinters. Leave the interior unfinished and omit an exterior perch.
tools_used: 50 mm hole saw with backing board
steps.safety: Clamp workpieces to a backing board and wear eye protection. Keep fingers away from the hole saw and rasp teeth.
steps.tip: A jigsaw can cut the entrance if a suitable hole saw is unavailable.

steps.title: Drill dowels and mark bracket positions
steps.text: Drill matching 6 mm dowel holes 15 mm deep in each mating surface: use heights 65, 200 and 360 mm for P2, and 65, 230 and 420 mm for P3. Dry-fit the walls and seat P5 on the slopes. Mark two interior bracket positions on each P1, approximately 70 and 170 mm behind the front, with each roof flange flush against P5's underside and its slot pointing across the roof grain. Mark and pilot-drill the side-face screw holes with a depth stop, then disassemble; do not drill holes through the roof.
tools_used: 6 mm doweling jig and drill depth stop
steps.safety: Clamp parts and wear eye protection. Limit pilot depth to avoid piercing visible wall faces.
steps.tip: Check bracket specifications before purchase; a slot running along the roof grain will not accommodate its main seasonal movement.

steps.title: Glue and square the walls
steps.text: Make J1 and J2 with twelve 6 x 30 mm hardwood dowels, three per corner, applying exterior glue to dowels and mating wall edges. Clamp P1 around P2 and P3 with all bottoms flush and both diagonals equal. Keep P4 out of the glue-up, remove interior squeeze-out, and recheck the floor opening after curing. Clamp for at least 60 minutes or the label minimum, and allow at least 24 hours before outdoor exposure.
steps.tip: Do not use the full-size fixed P4 as a tight assembly spacer; the corrected floor must withdraw freely after glue-up.

steps.title: Fit the external mounting cradle
steps.text: Complete J7 using one rear-and-side tree-mounting cradle kit rated for at least 15 kg, including its two straps and supplied attachment hardware. Attach it to P3 and both P1 broad faces according to its instructions, using the open top and bottom for access to any interior hardware. Keep all hardware clear of the roof brackets, wall dowels and floor withdrawal path. Leave the straps loose for installation.
steps.safety: Secure the box before drilling and wear eye protection. Check that no sharp fastener ends project into the nesting cavity.
steps.tip: Do not substitute a rear-only mounting kit for the specified cradle that mechanically connects the rear and side walls.

steps.title: Verify clearance and conditionally install the floor
steps.text: STOP here if P4 still has its fixed original dimensions: J3 has no seasonal clearance, so J4 and J5 must not be completed. After a separately approved floor correction, confirm approximately 2 mm clearance at all four edges and free downward withdrawal, then hold the floor underside flush with the wall bottoms. Locate retaining holes from its actual mid-thickness, approximately 40 mm from each front and rear wall side edge, and drill 7 mm deep head counterbores, wall clearance holes and floor-edge pilots. Without glue, drive two stainless 4 x 30 mm wood screws from the front and two from the rear to complete J4 and J5; perform this installation only after step 8 has secured the roof.
steps.safety: Support the box securely and wear eye protection. Use a depth stop for counterbores and pilots.
steps.tip: Step 7 is a clearance gate and preparation card; its final screw installation must wait until the open-bottom roof work in step 8 is finished.

steps.title: Secure the roof with side-grain bracket connections
steps.text: With P4 absent, complete J6 using four specified stainless slotted angle brackets: drive one 4 x 16 mm pan-head screw through each side flange into its prepared P1 broad-face pilot. Seat P5 on the slopes, making J8's unglued rear-top contact, and use the open top beside the temporarily shifted roof to mark shallow underside pilot holes through the roof-flange slot centers. Remove P5 to drill those pilots perpendicular to its underside, replace it, then reach through the open bottom to drive four more 4 x 16 mm pan-head screws, each with a 4 mm bore, 12 mm outside-diameter flat washer, through the bracket slots into P5. Apply no glue and seat washers only lightly against the bracket flanges so the roof can move across its grain; no screws penetrate the weather surface. Complete the conditional floor installation described in step 7 only after checking all four brackets.
steps.safety: Clamp the box securely and wear eye protection. Before fastening, verify at least 150 mm of straight driver clearance through the open bottom to every roof screw.
steps.tip: Use a hand screwdriver or long straight driver extension if needed; never substitute screws into P1's top end grain or drill vertically through the sloping roof.

steps.title: Inspect and mount only after the clearance issue is resolved
steps.text: Do not install the box outdoors until its floor geometry has been formally corrected, the floor withdraws freely, and all conditional assembly work is complete. Check the entrance, drainage, ventilation and roof hardware, then secure the already attached cradle's straps around a suitable tree according to the kit instructions. Select installation height and habitat for the intended species, and use a qualified installer if the location cannot be reached safely from the ground. Inspect straps regularly, loosen them for tree growth, and remove the box for cleaning only when unoccupied.
steps.safety: Do not climb while carrying the box or overreach from a ladder. Obtain assistance and suitable access equipment for elevated installation.
steps.tip: Leave cedar untreated; do not conceal the unresolved floor-clearance conflict by forcing the floor into place.

safety_overview: Wear eye protection during cutting, drilling and filing, hearing protection with power saws, and suitable dust protection when cutting cedar or plywood.
Clamp workpieces and use backing boards for hole-saw and through-drilling operations.
Use untreated wood, leave the interior unfinished, remove splinters and prevent sharp hardware from projecting into the nesting cavity.
Confirm the bird species before selecting entrance diameter, installation height and habitat; keep the ventilation and drainage openings clear.
Use a tree-friendly mounting kit rated for at least 15 kg, inspect it regularly, and never rely on loose wire or thin cord around a growing tree.
Avoid elevated DIY installation without appropriate access equipment and assistance; never disturb an occupied nest.

review.summary: The assembly sequence and tool access are workable, but the roof relies on screws into cedar end grain, and the snug removable floor needs seasonal clearance. Revise the roof attachment and weather sealing before building.

issues.problem: P1's grain runs vertically, so the vertically driven roof screws enter its sloping top edges substantially into end grain. This is a poor primary roof attachment in soft cedar, especially under wind uplift and repeated wetting.
issues.fix: Replace the direct roof-to-side-edge screws with interior roof cleats whose grain runs along the roof slope. Attach the cleats through P1's broad faces into the cleats' side grain before fitting P5. Fasten P5 into the cleats' side grain through movement slots, without glue. Add the cleats and their fasteners to the parts, joints, hardware and steps.

issues.problem: The screws are driven vertically while the roof surface slopes. Their pan heads and flat bonded washers therefore do not sit parallel to P5. Gentle tightening will not produce an even weather seal; tightening harder compromises the intended sliding attachment.
issues.fix: With the revised cleat attachment, drill and drive the roof screws perpendicular to P5 so the sealing washers seat flat. Retain slots across the roof grain and specify compatible screw lengths and washer seating instructions. Update J6 and step 8 together.

issues.problem: P4 is specified as a snug sliding fit with no seasonal clearance. The solid-cedar enclosure changes size across its grain outdoors, while the plywood floor changes much less. A floor that slides during dry assembly can become trapped, defeating the annual cleaning access.
issues.fix: Specify approximately 2 mm clearance at each floor edge rather than a snug fit. Cut P4 accordingly, check that it withdraws freely after wall glue-up, and locate the retaining holes from the fitted floor. Update J3, the P4 notes and steps 2, 5 and 7 to describe the clearance.

issues.problem: The roof may be purchased as an edge-glued cedar panel, but the plan does not require exterior-rated glue lines. An indoor project panel is not necessarily suitable for an exposed roof.
issues.fix: Specify either a single untreated cedar board or an edge-glued panel explicitly rated by its manufacturer for exterior exposure. Add this requirement to the roof purchasing notes.

plan.title: Slatted Timber Garden Bench with Arms
plan.summary: A two-person garden bench inspired by the photograph, with lengthwise seat slats, upright back slats, substantial legs and broad arms. Straight-cut components and glued dowel joints replace the photograph's curved arm details and concealed joinery.
assumptions: Dimensions are estimated from the photograph: 1400 mm overall width, 450 mm seat height and 900 mm back height.
The photograph does not reveal the entire frame or its joinery. This plan uses a new, buildable dowelled frame rather than claiming to reproduce the original construction.

Use straight, dry, exterior-suitable select pine, avoiding knots around joints. All stock sizes are finished actual dimensions; have a timber supplier prepare the 30 mm boards and 60 mm square posts if necessary.
The seat and back are flat rather than ergonomically curved. Arms are straight rectangular boards with eased edges rather than carved or curved components.
The intended service is two adults, up to approximately 200 kg combined, sitting normally. This is a design target, not a certified load rating; do not stand, jump or climb on the bench.
Use on a level, firm surface, preferably sheltered from prolonged rain. Exterior glue and a maintained exterior finish are necessary.
Dowels are purchased exterior-suitable hardwood fasteners. Do not substitute ordinary interior beech dowels for exposed outdoor service.

The bench is freestanding. Because its back exceeds 750 mm, consider anti-tip anchoring where children may climb or the site presents a tipping risk; substrate-specific anchoring is not included without site information.
Seat slats have 5 mm clearance from the legs at both ends. Slotted seat attachments allow seasonal movement without gluing the slats to the frame.
clarifying_questions: What overall bench width would fit your space?
Will the bench be fully exposed to rain or kept under cover?
Is the proposed 200 kg combined seating load sufficient?

parts.name: Front legs and arm posts
parts.notes: Continuous posts support both the seat frame and arms. Keep feet square and ease exposed edges without rounding joint faces.

parts.name: Rear legs and back posts
parts.notes: Continuous rear posts carry the backrest and receive the rear ends of the arms.

parts.name: Armrests
parts.notes: Grain runs front to back. Ease upper edges approximately 3 mm; retain square glue surfaces at the front post and rear-post connection.

parts.name: Front and rear seat-frame rails
parts.notes: Ends are dowelled into the inner faces of the legs. Three cross-bearers connect these rails and support the seat.

parts.name: Seat cross-bearers
parts.notes: The three bearers reduce the seat slat support spacing to 625 mm. Their tops align with the frame rails at y = 420 mm.

parts.name: Lengthwise seat slats
parts.notes: Leave 8 mm between slats. All six attach to all three bearers; only the first and last also contact the long frame rails. No glue at seat attachments.

parts.name: Upper and lower backrest rails
parts.notes: Rails fit between the rear posts. Back slats fit between the lower rail's upper edge and upper rail's lower edge.

parts.name: Vertical backrest slats
parts.notes: There are 44 mm gaps between slats, with 40 mm clearance to the left post and 44 mm to the right post. Slats are centered in the rails' 30 mm thickness.

joints.drive_from: Predrill rail ends and inward-facing front-post faces separately in step 2; slide the cured side units onto the rail-end dowels horizontally across the bench width in step 7.
joints.note: Front rail only. Centers are y = 345, 375 and 405 mm, z = 35 mm. Embed 30 mm in each member with a small glue-relief allowance. Glue dowels and mating faces. Assemble simultaneously with J2 and J4.

joints.drive_from: Predrill rail ends and inward-facing rear-post faces separately in step 2; slide the cured side units onto the rail-end dowels horizontally across the bench width in step 7.
joints.note: Rear seat-frame rail only. Centers are y = 345, 375 and 405 mm, z = 525 mm. Embed 30 mm in each member with glue relief. Glue dowels and mating faces. Assemble simultaneously with J1 and J4.

joints.drive_from: Predrill the inner faces of both long rails and both ends of each bearer while separate; bring the rails onto the bearer dowels and clamp front to back.
joints.note: Three bearers, two ends each. Centers are y = 360 and 390 mm at x = 75, 700 or 1325 mm. Embed 20 mm in each rail and 30 mm in each bearer, with minimal glue relief. These revised heights avoid intersecting J1 and J2 dowels. Glue dowels and mating faces.

joints.drive_from: Predrill rail ends and inward-facing rear-post faces while separate; slide the cured side units horizontally onto the supported backrest's rail-end dowels during the final widthwise assembly.
joints.note: Two dowels per rail end at z = 530 mm. Lower rail centers are y = 520 and 550 mm; upper rail centers are y = 850 and 880 mm. Embed 30 mm in each member with glue relief. Glue dowels and mating faces. Complete with J1 and J2, without spreading or bending cured side units.

joints.drive_from: Predrill slat ends and facing rail edges while separate; assemble flat on padded supports and clamp along the slat lengths.
joints.note: Two dowels at each slat end, positioned 20 and 60 mm across its width and centered at z = 530 mm. Embed 20 mm in each member with glue relief. Glue dowels and mating faces. Cure this panel before the final frame assembly.

joints.drive_from: Predrill arm undersides and front-post tops while separate; engage the arm-to-front-post dowels first in the flat side-unit jig, before fitting either rear post.
joints.note: Centers are 15 and 45 mm across each arm at z = 30 mm. Embed 20 mm into the arm and 30 mm into the post. Glue the contact area and dowels. After this joint is seated, slide P2 onto J7 horizontally along the arm.

joints.drive_from: Predrill arm rear ends and forward-facing rear-post faces while separate; after seating J6, slide each free rear post forward onto its arm-end dowels in the flat side-unit jig.
joints.note: Centers are 15 and 45 mm across each arm at y = 655 mm. Embed 30 mm into each member with glue relief. Glue dowels and mating faces. Keep front and rear posts parallel with 440 mm between their facing surfaces; cure each complete side unit before step 7.

joints.drive_from: From above through each seat slat into each bearer's top edge, after the complete frame has cured and before finishing.
joints.note: One screw per slat at each of x = 75, 700 and 1325 mm. Front-to-back screw positions for the six slats are z = 90, 148, 236, 324, 412 and 470 mm respectively; the first and last positions avoid J3 dowels. Use 6 mm round clearance holes over the center bearer and 6 x 12 mm slots along z over the outer bearers. No glue. Predrill receiving wood and seat washers without locking the slots. Approximately 40 mm of each screw enters the bearer.

joints.drive_from: From above through the first and last seat slats into the long frame rails, after the complete frame has cured.
joints.note: Front slat to front rail: x = 300, 500 and 1100 mm, z = 35 mm. Rear slat to rear rail: the same x positions at z = 525 mm. The revised middle position avoids the center bearer's J3 dowels. Use 6 x 12 mm slots along z, washers and no glue. Predrill receiving rails; approximately 40 mm of each screw enters the rail.

joints.drive_from: Apply a thin film of exterior glue to the small contact patches before sliding the side units inward in step 7; clamp across the bench width.
joints.note: Incidental glued face contact, not an independent structural support joint. Each outer bearer's outward face contacts its front post over y = 330–420 mm and z = 50–60 mm, at x = 60 or 1340 mm. No fasteners fit safely within this narrow patch. Structural loads are carried by J1 and J3; glue this contact when making those surrounding joints.

joints.drive_from: Apply a thin film of exterior glue to the small contact patches before sliding the side units inward in step 7; clamp across the bench width.
joints.note: Incidental glued face contact, not an independent structural support joint. Each outer bearer's outward face contacts its rear post over y = 330–420 mm and z = 500–510 mm, at x = 60 or 1340 mm. No fasteners fit safely within this narrow patch. Structural loads are carried by J2 and J3; glue this contact when making those surrounding joints.

consumables.note: Choose a waterproof product specifically approved for exterior furniture and the selected species; follow its open time and cure instructions.

consumables.name: Sandpaper

consumables.name: End-grain exterior sealer

consumables.name: Disposable brushes and wiping cloths

Miter saw
tools.alternative: Use a sharp handsaw and guide block, or have the timber supplier make square crosscuts.

tools.name: Drill/driver with 8 mm and 10 mm wood bits, pilot bit and depth stops
tools.alternative: A hand drill can be used with the same dowelling guides and depth stops.

tools.name: Self-centering dowelling jig and dowel transfer centers
tools.alternative: Use an accurate shop-made drilling guide with hardened bushings and test it on scrap first.

tools.name: Long bar or pipe clamps
tools.alternative: Use rated woodworking strap clamps with protective corner blocks; arrange separate clamps for the backrest.

tools.name: Random-orbit sander
tools.alternative: Use a sanding block and sand with the grain.

tools.name: Small round file and 6 mm drill bit
tools.alternative: Use a small router with a suitable guide to form the seat slots before assembly.

tools.name: Work supports and protective clamping blocks
tools.alternative: Use a stable workbench and padded scrap blocks.

steps.title: Obtain finished-width stock and crosscut
steps.text: Have the timber supplier machine every P1–P8 component to its listed finished width and thickness, including the 60 mm square posts; only square crosscuts to length remain for you. Crosscut using a miter saw, or a sharp handsaw and guide block, then label each copy and its reference faces. Reject stock with splits, large knots or severe grain runout near joints.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil and combination square
Work supports and protective clamping blocks
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection for powered cutting, use dust extraction and respiratory protection, and support long stock. Keep hands clear of the cutting path.
steps.tip: Do not attempt lengthwise ripping with a miter saw; order all finished widths from the supplier.

steps.title: Drill the dowel holes and seat slots
steps.text: Use the dowelling jig and depth stops to drill J1–J7 at the corrected locations in the joints array, testing each setup on scrap first. In particular, J3 uses two 10 x 50 mm dowels per bearer end at heights 360 and 390 mm, avoiding the rail-to-post dowels. Prepare P6 clearance holes and movement slots using the revised J8 and J9 screw positions, but do not drive screws yet. Leave the narrow J10 and J11 contact patches undrilled.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil and combination square
Drill/driver with 8 mm and 10 mm wood bits, pilot bit and depth stops
Self-centering dowelling jig and dowel transfer centers
Small round file and 6 mm drill bit
steps.safety: Clamp every workpiece, wear eye protection and use depth stops to prevent breakthrough. Keep fingers clear of rotating bits.
steps.tip: Reference every mating hole from the same marked face; the final assembly requires all rail-end dowels to align at once.

steps.title: Rehearse the assembly and sand
steps.text: With removable test dowels and a helper, dry-fit the P4/P5 seat frame and P7/P8 backrest separately, then each P1/P3/P2 side unit: seat J6 first and only then slide the rear post onto J7. Support the seat frame and backrest at their finished heights and rehearse sliding both complete side units inward across the width onto J1, J2 and J4 without bending or spreading them. Check four-foot contact, matching diagonals, 8 mm seat gaps and 5 mm seat end clearances, then disassemble. Sand exposed surfaces through 120–180 grit and ease exposed edges approximately 3 mm, keeping joint faces flat and bare.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil and combination square
Work supports and protective clamping blocks
steps.safety: Use dust extraction, eye protection and a dust mask when sanding. Have a helper stabilize all loose assemblies and keep fingers out of closing joints.
steps.tip: Mark temporary support and spacer positions now; do not proceed to glue until the exact final widthwise assembly works smoothly.

steps.title: Glue and cure the seat-frame subassembly
steps.text: Make J3 by joining the three P5 bearers between the two P4 rails, using two glued 10 x 50 mm exterior hardwood dowels at each of the six ends, twelve dowels total. Apply exterior glue to dowels, holes and mating faces, then clamp front to back on a flat surface with all tops flush at the future 420 mm height. Check matching diagonals and the specified bearer positions before tightening. Keep clamped at least 60 minutes and allow 24 hours cure, or the glue label's longer times, before handling it for final assembly; do not attach any posts yet.
tools_used: Work supports and protective clamping blocks
Tape measure, pencil and combination square
steps.safety: Support both long rails and keep fingers away from the closing bearer joints. Lift the cured frame with a helper if needed.
steps.tip: The outer bearers must finish flush with the rail ends at x = 60 and 1340 mm.

steps.title: Glue and cure the backrest panel
steps.text: Lay P7 rails and all ten P8 slats on padded supports at the specified positions, leaving 44 mm between adjacent slats. Make J5 with two glued 8 x 40 mm exterior hardwood dowels at each slat end, forty dowels total, applying glue to holes, dowels and mating faces. Clamp along the slat lengths and check that the panel is flat and square. Keep clamped at least 60 minutes and allow 24 hours cure, or the glue label's longer times, before final assembly.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil and combination square
Work supports and protective clamping blocks
steps.safety: Support the entire panel and keep hands clear of closing rail-to-slat joints.
steps.tip: Leave the rail-end holes for J4 clean and free of hardened glue.

steps.title: Glue and cure the two side units
steps.text: Lay each P1/P3/P2 side unit on a flat jig, using temporary clamped spacers to keep its posts parallel, their feet on one baseline and their facing surfaces 440 mm apart. First make J6 by seating P3 onto P1 with two glued 8 x 50 mm dowels, then make J7 by sliding the still-free P2 forward onto the arm's two glued 8 x 60 mm rear dowels. Glue all mating faces and holes, and clamp both connections while checking the arm underside is 640 mm above the foot baseline and the rear post projects to 900 mm. Use four dowels of each size across both side units, keep clamped at least 60 minutes and allow 24 hours cure or the label's longer times, then remove the temporary spacers.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil and combination square
Work supports and protective clamping blocks
steps.safety: Keep the side units fully supported and fingers clear of the sliding rear posts and closing joints. Temporary jig blocks must be clamped securely.
steps.tip: Do not connect the rear arm dowels first: that would prevent the arm from moving onto the front post's vertical dowels.

steps.title: Join the cured subassemblies across the width
steps.text: With a helper, support the cured P4/P5 seat frame with its top at 420 mm and the cured P7/P8 panel with its lower edge at 500 mm, and repeat the widthwise dry run with both cured side units before applying glue. Make J1 and J2 using three glued 10 x 60 mm dowels at each of four seat-rail ends, twelve total, and J4 using two glued 10 x 60 mm dowels at each of four back-rail ends, eight total; glue all dowels, holes and mating faces. Apply a thin glue film to the two narrow P1/P5 contact patches for J10 and the two P2/P5 patches for J11, with no additional fasteners, then slide both side units inward along x onto all rail-end dowels together. Clamp across the width, check matching diagonals and four-foot contact, and keep clamped at least 60 minutes with 24 hours cure or the label's longer requirements before removing supports or loading.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil and combination square
Work supports and protective clamping blocks
steps.safety: Use a helper and stable supports throughout; never balance the backrest unsupported. Keep fingers clear of all closing joints and do not sit on the uncured frame.
steps.tip: Choose exterior glue with enough published working time for the rehearsed operation; never force a cured side unit to spread or twist.

steps.title: Fasten the seat with movement allowance
steps.text: After full frame cure, position P6 with 8 mm gaps and 5 mm end clearances, then pilot-drill the receiving wood at the corrected J8 and J9 locations. Make J8 from above with one 5 x 70 mm stainless pan-head screw and one 5 mm washer at each of eighteen slat-to-bearer contacts, using z = 90 mm on the first slat and z = 470 mm on the last to avoid bearer dowels. Make J9 from above with three identical screws and washers into each long rail, six more screws total, at x = 300, 500 and 1100 mm. Use no glue beneath the seat and tighten only until washers seat without crushing the wood or preventing movement in the slots.
tools_used: Drill/driver with 8 mm and 10 mm wood bits, pilot bit and depth stops
Tape measure, pencil and combination square
steps.safety: Wear eye protection, clamp slats while drilling and use pilot-depth stops. Do not overdrive screws or leave sharp, raised hardware edges.
steps.tip: J8 holes over the center bearer are round; its outer-bearer holes and every J9 hole are slotted front to back.

steps.title: Seal and finish the bench
steps.text: Remove dried glue residue, lightly sand rough spots and remove dust. Apply compatible exterior end-grain sealer to exposed ends, especially the feet, then apply exterior furniture stain to all accessible faces, including the underside and between slats. Allow approximately 24 hours between coats and at least 72 hours before use unless the product specifies longer; keep the bench sheltered while drying.
steps.safety: Use gloves, ventilation and respiratory protection as required by the finish label, plus dust protection for sanding. Manage oily cloths according to the label to prevent spontaneous combustion.
steps.tip: Test the dark weathered color underneath first and keep finish buildup out of movement slots.

steps.title: Inspect and place the bench
steps.text: With a helper, place the cured bench on a firm, level surface and check for rocking, open joints, splinters and protruding fasteners. Apply seating weight gradually while observing the joints, stopping immediately if anything shifts, opens or creaks persistently. Do not exceed the provisional 200 kg combined seating target, and inspect joints and finish each season; assess site-specific anti-tip anchoring where children might climb on the 900 mm back.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil and combination square
steps.safety: Lift with two people, keep fingers clear beneath the feet and never stand or climb on the bench. A gradual seating check is not a certified structural load test.
steps.tip: Keep the feet out of standing water and renew the exterior finish before the wood begins absorbing water.

safety_overview: Wear eye protection for cutting and drilling, hearing protection around power saws, and respiratory protection when producing wood dust.
Clamp stock before drilling or cutting; support long pieces and use depth stops to prevent drilling through visible faces.
Use a helper during the large frame glue-up and when lifting or moving the finished bench.
Allow structural glue and finish to cure fully before use; stop using the bench if joints open, screws loosen or timber splits.
Use exterior finishes with ventilation and manage oily cloths as a fire hazard.
Use only on level ground, do not climb or stand on the bench, and assess anti-tip anchoring where children or site conditions create a tipping risk.

review.summary: The dowelled frame and supported seat are reasonable construction choices, but the main glue-up needs a workable, unambiguous assembly sequence. The stock-preparation instructions also require a ripping method that is not currently listed.

issues.problem: Steps 4–7 do not provide a reliable assembly sequence. Step 4 starts the frame glue-up, but step 5 then requires at least an hour of backrest clamping before that still-workable frame is needed. The tips contradict the numbered order. Step 7 also says to engage the horizontal rear-arm dowels and then lower the arms onto vertical front-post dowels; fully engaged rear dowels prevent that lowering motion. Leaving clamps loose does not itself provide the necessary movement.
issues.fix: Rewrite the numbered sequence around separate subassemblies: first glue and cure the P7/P8 backrest and the P4/P5 seat frame. Then assemble each P1/P3/P2 side unit, engaging J6 before sliding the rear post onto J7; use a flat jig and temporary spacers to maintain the required post spacing and alignment. Once these units have cured, bring both side units onto the seat-frame and backrest rail-end dowels in one widthwise glue-up, completing J1, J2 and J4 together. Dry-run that exact sequence with a helper before applying glue, and update the joint step references.

issues.problem: Step 1 tells the builder to cut boards to width, but the listed miter saw and its handsaw crosscut alternative do not provide a suitable method for ripping these long components. The supplier-preparation assumption discusses thicknesses and posts without clearly requiring every board to arrive at its finished width.

plan.title: Painted Spindle-Back Dining Chair
plan.summary: A sturdy, yellow-painted wooden chair inspired by the photograph, with a thick shaped seat, three back spindles and a curved crest rail. Straight legs and a reinforced apron frame replace the photograph's uncertain turned and splayed construction, making this an achievable intermediate build.
assumptions: The close-up photograph does not show the complete chair or its hidden joinery. Overall size is estimated as an adult dining chair with a 450 mm seat height.
This interpretation preserves the thick seat, yellow finish, spindles and shaped crest, but uses straight square legs rather than reproducing uncertain turned or splayed parts.
Use clear, straight-grained poplar or maple for the frame and a sound 38 mm edge-glued solid-wood seat panel; do not use construction lumber with knots in structural members.
The seat grain runs left to right. Its rear spindle line acts as its fixed movement reference; figure-eight fasteners allow the remainder of the seat to move seasonally.
The crest is flat in depth with a curved upper silhouette, not steam-bent or carved. Its grain runs left to right.
The plan is intended for ordinary single-adult seating, approximately 100 kg maximum intended occupant mass, but is not an independently tested or certified load rating. Never stand on the chair.
Rear seat notches provide 2 mm clearance from the rear posts. Outline coordinates describe the seat in plan view and the crest in front view.
Hardware is represented in the joints, not as separate wooden parts. Follow the selected figure-eight kit's recess and pilot-hole requirements.
clarifying_questions: Is this intended as an adult dining chair or a smaller child's chair?
Do you want this simpler square-leg interpretation, or is reproducing the turned, splayed appearance essential?

steps.title: Select stock and make a full-size layout
steps.text: Inspect P1–P8 stock and reject splits, loose knots and severe grain runout. Draw the seat and frame positions full size, checking the 450 mm seat height, 850 mm overall height and left-to-right seat grain. Keep all listed external part dimensions unchanged; the corrected crest connection uses concealed 12 mm upper spindle tenons rather than full-diameter upper sockets.
tools_used: Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.tip: Do not use finger-jointed decorative trim for structural legs or back posts.

steps.title: Cut the frame and shaped parts
steps.text: Cut P1–P5 and P7 to their listed dimensions with square ends. Cut P6's notches and rounded front outline, then cut P8's curved upper outline from its 324 x 110 x 25 mm blank. Keep P5's grain vertical in the finished chair and ease exposed edges approximately 3 mm without rounding joint faces.
tools_used: Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection for powered cutting, clamp work securely and control dust. A guided handsaw and coping saw can replace the powered saws.
steps.tip: Leave the spindle upper ends square at this stage; their reduced tenons are formed in step 4.

steps.title: Drill the structural dowel holes
steps.text: Use the 8 mm jig to drill two holes at each apron end and matching leg face, providing 20 mm nominal embedment per member plus a little extra drilling depth for glue clearance. Front/rear apron holes are at assembled heights 342 and 382 mm; side-apron holes are at 352 and 392 mm. Drill P8 and its matching P2 faces at heights 765 and 800 mm, centered at z406 mm, and label every mating pair.
tools_used: 8 mm doweling jig and depth stops
Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.safety: Clamp every part, wear eye protection and use depth stops. Clear chips with the drill stopped.
steps.tip: The staggered apron-hole heights keep perpendicular dowels from colliding inside the legs.

steps.title: Prepare spindle joinery and preinstall seat hardware
steps.text: Drill three 22 mm diameter, 18 mm deep sockets in P6 at x120, 225 and 330 mm, all at z406 mm. Using a guided 12 mm round-tenon cutter, reduce only the uppermost 18 mm of each P7 to a concentric 12 mm tenon with a square shoulder, retaining its 326 mm overall length; alternatively, have a woodworking shop form these tenons. Drill matching 12 mm diameter, 18 mm deep sockets into P8's bottom edge on the same centerlines, replacing the earlier 22 mm crest-socket instruction, and test for a snug hand fit. Prepare flush figure-eight recesses in P3 and P4 at 100 mm from both ends, then immediately install all eight plates with their eight included 20–25 mm apron-side screws driven downward into pilots while the top edges remain uncovered. Set the seat-side lobes inward, verify free pivoting and assembly clearance, and reserve the eight seat-side screws for step 9.
tools_used: 12 mm brad-point bit and depth stop
Pilot bits, countersink and screwdriver bits
Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.safety: Clamp the crest in a stable cradle and clamp spindles against rotation when using the tenon cutter. Wear eye protection and follow the cutter manufacturer's speed and holding instructions.
steps.tip: Do not simply drill smaller sockets for unmodified spindle ends, and do not drill 22 mm sockets into the 25 mm crest.

steps.title: Rehearse assembly and glue the separate front frame
steps.text: Rehearse steps 6 and 7 completely without glue: support P6, fit the spindles and crest, close the rear posts around the rear apron and crest, then connect that rear assembly to the separate front frame using P4. Check the 2 mm rear-post clearances, shoulder seating and movement-hardware clearance, then disassemble and sand accessible surfaces through 180 grit. Make J1 by gluing the front P3 apron between both P1 legs with two 8 x 40 mm dowels per end, four total. Clamp square for at least 60 minutes and allow 24 hours before joining this front frame to the rear assembly.
tools_used: Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.safety: Control sanding dust and support loose posts against falling. Use stable temporary supports during the rehearsal.
steps.tip: Never force misaligned dowels with clamps; correct their alignment before applying glue.

steps.title: Build and cure the supported seat-and-rear assembly
steps.text: Keep the front frame and both P4 side aprons separate, and independently support P6 level with its underside at y412 mm. Make J8 by gluing the three full-diameter P7 lower ends 18 mm into P6, then lower P8 vertically onto their glued 12 mm upper tenons to make J9, with each shoulder seated and 290 mm of spindle exposed. Make J2 and J7 by closing both P2 posts horizontally around the rear P3 apron and P8, using two glued 8 x 40 mm dowels at each of these four joints, eight total. Maintain the unglued 2 mm seat-notch clearances at J15, keep the seat unglued to the rear apron and verify the rear posts are parallel. Clamp at least 60 minutes, keep the seat independently supported and allow 24 hours of cure before the next assembly.
tools_used: Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.safety: Use a helper to control the posts and clamps. The rear assembly is not freestanding; keep it braced and never load the supported seat.
steps.tip: Lower the crest onto the spindles before installing either rear post; no perpendicular dowel closures should be attempted simultaneously.

steps.title: Connect the cured front and rear assemblies
steps.text: Keep P6 independently supported and insert both P4 side aprons into the rear posts, then slide the separate front frame rearward onto their front ends. Make J3 and J4 with two glued 8 x 40 mm dowels at each of the four joints, eight total, closing all joints along the same front-to-back axis. Let P6 bear dry on the front-leg tops to make J12, and register the four apron-edge contacts J16 without glue or extra fasteners. Check equal frame diagonals and four-foot contact, clamp for at least 60 minutes and allow 24 hours before proceeding; the seat remains unfastened to the aprons until step 9.
tools_used: Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.safety: Keep the seat supported until the frame is secure, and use a helper when moving the assembly. Keep fingers clear of closing joints.
steps.tip: Do not spread the cured front or rear frame to insert an apron; both side aprons must close in the same direction.

steps.title: Reinforce all four apron corners
steps.text: From the open underside, position each P5 block 10 mm below P6, applying glue only to its two apron-contact faces; J13 and J14 are incidental leg-edge contacts with no glue or fasteners. Make J5 with two 4 x 50 mm screws per block driven through P3, eight total, pairing the 20 mm offset from the leg with y374 mm and the 45 mm offset with y392 mm. Make J6 with another two 4 x 50 mm screws per block driven through P4, eight total, pairing the 20 mm offset with y382 mm and the 45 mm offset with y398 mm. Clamp blocks, drill apron clearance holes and block pilots, countersink the outside heads and keep the blocks unglued to the seat. Leave clamps on for at least 60 minutes and allow the glue to cure as labeled.
tools_used: Pilot bits, countersink and screwdriver bits
steps.safety: Secure the chair before accessing its underside, wear eye protection and use drilling-depth stops. Keep hands away from screw paths.
steps.tip: Measure offsets along each apron from the adjacent leg face; the staggered screw heights prevent perpendicular screws from colliding.

steps.title: Complete the seat fastenings from underneath
steps.text: Pad and secure the chair on its side, exposing its open underside. Complete J10 and J11 by driving only the eight reserved 20–25 mm seat-side screws upward through the eight preinstalled figure-eight plates into predrilled P6 pilots: four screws through the P3 hardware and four through the P4 hardware. Do not attempt to install or redrive downward-facing apron-side screws here; those were installed with clear access in step 4. Use no glue, retain free plate pivoting and verify at least half of each screw's length enters the receiving wood while its tip remains at least 3 mm below the seat's upper face.
tools_used: Pilot bits, countersink and screwdriver bits
steps.safety: Secure the chair against rolling and use depth stops. Keep at least 150 mm of straight driver access by working through the open frame with an extension if necessary.
steps.tip: The solid seat must remain free to change depth seasonally; do not substitute rigid brackets or glue it to the frame.

steps.title: Inspect the assembly and prepare for paint
steps.text: After all structural glue has cured, inspect the joints for gaps or movement and check that all four feet sit on a flat floor. Fill recessed apron screw heads, let the filler dry as labeled and sand repaired areas through 180 grit. Remove dust, check that seat clearances remain open and lightly ease any remaining sharp contact edges.
tools_used: Tape measure, square and marking pencil
steps.safety: Wear dust protection while sanding. Do not stand on the chair, drop onto it or test it by rocking onto two legs.
steps.tip: Any cracking or joint movement requires structural repair before use; filler is not a structural repair.

steps.title: Apply the yellow finish and allow full cure
steps.text: Apply one compatible primer coat followed by two thin coats of yellow waterborne furniture enamel, including accessible undersides. Allow approximately 4 hours for primer and 6 hours between enamel coats, or longer if the product label requires it. Keep paint out of the figure-eight pivots and rear-post clearance gaps. Allow the manufacturer's full service cure, commonly 7 days, before regular seated use.
steps.safety: Ventilate the work area and follow coating-label PPE and disposal instructions. Keep children away until the finish has cured.
steps.tip: Use a warm golden yellow with a modest sheen to approximate the photograph.

safety_overview: Wear eye protection for cutting and drilling, hearing protection for powered saws, and suitable dust protection when sanding.
Clamp narrow rails and round stock before drilling; never hold them loose against a large bit.
Use only sound structural timber and accurately fitted glued joints; cosmetic filler cannot repair a loose chair joint.
Allow structural glue and paint to cure fully before use, and inspect the chair periodically for looseness.
Use the chair on a level floor for seated use only; do not stand on it or rock back onto two legs.

plan.title: Two-Step Stool with Curved Treads
plan.summary: A sturdy interpretation of the photographed stool, with honey-colored curved treads and a dark, shaped base. Two plywood side frames and four crossrails support the steps; glued dowels and pocket screws provide structural connections without relying on screws into end grain.
assumptions: Dimensions are estimated from the photograph: 460 mm wide, 480 mm deep and 450 mm high, with the lower tread at 225 mm.
The photograph does not reveal the original joints. This version substitutes shaped plywood side frames and reinforced crossrails for the apparently solid-wood construction.
Use measured 24 mm birch plywood throughout. If purchased plywood differs in thickness, recalculate rail lengths and dowel depths before cutting.
The natural treads and dark base approximate the photograph; exposed plywood edges will remain visible.
Intended for one adult up to approximately 90 kg on a level indoor floor. This is a conservative design target, not a tested or certified load rating.
The upper platform is for standing, not for use as a chair. Do not add height, use on stairs, or use as a substitute for a ladder.
A half sheet of 24 mm birch plywood should accommodate the parts with careful layout; availability and pricing vary.
clarifying_questions: What finished height and maximum user weight should the stool accommodate?
Are visible plywood edges acceptable, or do you want a solid-wood version closer to the original?

steps.title: Lay out the parts
steps.text: Measure the plywood thickness before marking P1 (side frames), P2 (upper platform), P3 (lower tread), P4 (upper rails) and P5 (lower rails). Lay out the rectangular blanks with the tread face grain running left-to-right and allow for saw kerfs. Mark each part's inside face and front edge.
steps.tip: If the sheet is not 24 mm thick, do not simply use these rail lengths unchanged.

steps.title: Cut the rectangular blanks
steps.text: Cut all five part types to their listed rectangular sizes using a supported straightedge. Keep the two P1 blanks identical and verify that all four rail ends are square. Have the supplier make these cuts if handling sheet goods is difficult.
steps.safety: Support the sheet and offcuts, keep hands away from the cut line, and wear eye, hearing and dust protection.
steps.tip: Cut a little outside the line only where you intend to trim or sand afterward.

steps.title: Shape the frames and treads
steps.text: Transfer the P1 outline onto both side frames, remembering that its first profile coordinate is height and its second is depth. Mark and cut the shallow curves on P2 and P3 using the supplied profiles. Fair the curves with a rasp and sanding block, and ease exposed edges by about 2 mm while preserving flat glue-bearing edges.
steps.safety: Clamp each blank securely, keep the blade clear of the bench, and wear eye, hearing and dust protection.
steps.tip: Check both side frames together on a flat surface; unequal feet will make the stool rock.

steps.title: Prepare and dry-fit the joinery
steps.text: Drill two pocket holes at each end of every P4 and P5 rail: a pocket hole is an angled hole that lets a screw enter the adjoining side face. Test the jig and 40 mm screws on scrap before loosely clamping the base at its final dimensions. Using the joint coordinates, drill 8 mm dowel holes 16 mm deep in all bearing edges and matching tread undersides, then dry-fit with removable test dowels.
tools_used: Pocket-hole jig suitable for 24 mm material
8 mm doweling jig, dowel centers and depth stop
steps.safety: Clamp parts before drilling, use a positive depth stop, and wear eye protection.
steps.tip: Do not force a dry fit with all fluted dowels fully inserted; they can be difficult to remove.

steps.title: Sand and color the parts
steps.text: Sand P1 through P5 to 180-grit, taking care not to cut through the plywood face veneer. Mask every mating glue surface and dowel hole, then stain P1, P4 and P5 dark and P2 and P3 honey-colored. Let the stain dry at least 4 hours, or longer if its label requires, and remove the masking before assembly.
steps.safety: Use dust extraction and a respirator while sanding; ventilate during staining and follow the product's handling and disposal instructions.
steps.tip: Clean, unstained wood at the glue surfaces is essential for strong joints.

steps.title: Assemble the reinforced base
steps.text: Clamp P4 and P5 between the two P1 frames with rail tops at 426 mm and 201 mm respectively, and apply glue to all eight rail-end contacts. Drive two 40 mm coarse-thread pocket screws at each connection from the inward-facing rail faces, for 16 screws total. Work with the base on its side, use the long driver extension along the rail span, check square, and leave clamped for at least 60 minutes or the glue maker's stated time.
steps.safety: Secure the assembly against rolling and keep fingers clear of clamp pads and rotating bits.
steps.tip: Do not install either tread yet; the open top is needed for driver access.

steps.title: Glue on the lower tread
steps.text: Attach P3 to the lower bearing edges of P1 and the tops of P5 using twelve 8 x 30 mm fluted hardwood dowels: four per side frame and two per rail. Apply glue to the dowels, hole walls and all contacting bearing surfaces, then lower the tread straight down. Clamp through scrap cauls until every bearing edge closes tightly, and leave clamped at least 60 minutes or as directed by the glue label.
steps.tip: Stop and correct misalignment rather than hammering the tread onto incorrectly positioned dowels.

steps.title: Glue on the upper platform
steps.text: Attach P2 to the upper bearing edges of P1 and the tops of P4 using twelve 8 x 30 mm fluted hardwood dowels: four per side frame and two per rail. Glue the dowels, hole walls and all mating bearing surfaces, then clamp with protective cauls for at least 60 minutes. Leave the complete stool unloaded for at least 24 hours, or longer if the glue label specifies.
steps.tip: Check that P2 is level and that its left and right overhangs are equal before tightening the clamps.

steps.title: Apply the protective finish
steps.text: Remove glue squeeze-out without sanding through the stain, and lightly smooth any raised grain with 220-grit paper. Apply three thin coats of compatible water-based floor-rated satin finish to all exposed surfaces, including the undersides and feet. Allow about 3 hours between coats only if permitted by the label, and follow its longer drying requirements when conditions are cool or humid.
steps.safety: Ventilate, wear the finish manufacturer's recommended protection, and keep the drying stool away from children and ignition sources.
steps.tip: A heavy glossy coating can make a step slippery; do not substitute furniture polish or wax.

steps.title: Add traction to both steps
steps.text: Apply compatible clear anti-slip tread coating to the upper walking faces of P2 and P3 according to its label. Keep the coating even and preserve clearly visible tread edges. Allow the complete finish system to reach full service cure, commonly 5–7 days but determined by the products used.
steps.safety: Ventilate during application and do not stand on the stool before the coating has fully cured.
steps.tip: Test the coating and clear-finish combination on scrap first.

steps.title: Inspect before use
steps.text: Set the stool on a hard, level floor and verify that all four feet bear evenly and every joint remains tightly closed. Check for rocking, cracks, loose screws and slippery tread surfaces; correct any defect before use. Apply weight gradually using secured weights while standing beside the stool, stopping immediately at movement or noise; this check does not certify a load rating.
steps.safety: Keep people clear of test weights, do not use your body as the initial test load, and never jump on or lean beyond the footprint of the stool.
steps.tip: Inspect the stool periodically and retire it from use if plywood delamination, cracking or joint movement appears.

safety_overview: Wear eye and hearing protection for cutting and drilling, and use dust extraction with a suitable respirator when sanding plywood.
Clamp work securely and support sheet goods and offcuts; keep hands clear of blades and drill bits.
Use only sound, void-free plywood at structural connections; reject delaminated material or damaged edges.
Let glue and finishes fully cure, provide slip-resistant walking surfaces, and inspect all joints before use.
Use on a dry, level indoor floor with one person only; do not jump, overreach, place on another platform, or exceed the assumed 90 kg design target.

review.summary: The assembly sequence preserves drilling and driver access, and the supported, doweled treads and reinforced plywood base provide a reasonable construction approach. Materials and techniques are suitable for an intermediate builder, with appropriate curing, traction and safety instructions. No major buildability or durability issues found; the stated 90 kg capacity remains an unverified design target, not a certified rating.

plan.title: Classroom-Style Chair with Attached Writing Desk
plan.summary: Build one right-handed student chair-and-desk unit inspired by the photograph: a woodgrain writing surface, red seat and back, and black supports. This workshop-friendly version substitutes a rigid plywood structure for the photograph's welded tubular steel and molded seat. It is a visual adaptation, not an exact replica or certified institutional chair.
assumptions: The project is one integrated student chair and right-handed writing desk, rather than the entire classroom arrangement.
Dimensions are estimated from the photograph: seat height 450 mm, writing height 740 mm, and back height 820 mm.
The seat is 494 mm wide and 422 mm deep. Entry is from the left, behind the front writing surface.
Use furniture-grade 18 mm birch plywood with sound cores, not MDF, particleboard, or sheathing plywood.
A flat plywood seat and back replace the photograph's molded, curved components. The plywood support panels are deliberately more substantial than the original steel frame.
A straight-grained 38 x 64 mm hardwood front leg is used; its grain runs vertically.
The design is intended for ordinary seated use by one person. It has no verified load rating and is not a substitute for tested school furniture.
The footprint requires approximately one 1220 x 2440 mm plywood sheet with a carefully planned cutting layout.
Finish thickness and minor edge easing are excluded from the geometry.
clarifying_questions: Is this for a child or an adult, and what is the intended user's approximate height and weight?
Do you want right-handed entry as shown here, or a mirrored left-handed version?
Is a plywood adaptation acceptable, or is matching the original tubular-steel frame essential?

joints.note: Glue the 82 mm contacting edge section. Pocket centers are at y = 370 and 410 mm; keep these holes clear of the seat pockets.

joints.note: Glue the rear seat edge. Pocket centers are at x = 85, 205, 325, and 445 mm.

joints.note: Glue the apron end. Pocket centers are at y = 570, 625, and 680 mm. Screws enter the leg across its grain, not through its end.

joints.drive_from: From the rear face of P6 into the inside broad face of P1, before attaching P7.
joints.note: Glue the apron end. Pocket centers are at y = 570, 625, and 680 mm. Keep apron and P1 front edges flush.

joints.drive_from: From the inside face of P1 upward into the underside of P7, with the assembly supported upside down.
joints.note: Glue the contacting top edge for z = 0 to 500 mm only. Pocket centers are at z = 80, 220, and 420 mm. Both components are plywood, so this glued connection does not constrain solid-wood movement.

joints.drive_from: From the rear face of P6 upward into the underside of P7, with the assembly supported upside down.
joints.note: Glue the top apron edge. Pocket centers are at x = 120, 270, and 420 mm, clear of end-joint pockets.

joints.drive_from: From a pocket in the left exterior face of P5 upward into the underside of P7.
joints.note: Glue the leg's top end. Center the pocket at z = 42 mm to avoid the apron screws. The narrow leg section does not present a wide cross-grain movement issue.
