steps.title: Confirm fit and mark the cutting layout
steps.text: Mock up a 450 mm seat height and 740 mm writing height before cutting. Mark P1 through P7 on the plywood, allowing for your saw's kerf, and mark P5 on the hardwood. Confirm the user can enter from the left and sit comfortably behind the 280 mm-deep front writing area.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil, and combination square
steps.tip: Adjust the plan before cutting if the intended user needs a different seat or writing height; do not simply shorten isolated parts.

steps.title: Cut the blanks and shaped outlines
steps.text: Cut P1 through P7 to their listed bounding dimensions. Cut the two upper corners of P4 and the rear-left opening in P7 to the supplied profiles, supporting both sides of each cut. Keep P1, P2, P5, and P6 square so their floor and top edges align.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil, and combination square
steps.safety: Wear eye, hearing, and respiratory protection. Clamp work securely, support offcuts, and keep hands outside the blade path.
steps.tip: Label the front, rear, inside, and underside faces immediately after cutting.

steps.title: Drill pockets and dry-fit the structure
steps.text: A pocket hole is an angled hole that lets a screw enter the broad face of the adjoining part. Drill the pockets for J1 through J10 at the locations in the joint notes, using 18 mm settings for plywood and the jig's 38 mm-to-18 mm mixed-thickness guidance for P5. Test 32 mm screws on matching scraps, checking that the receiving-face clearance is at least 3 mm and that the pockets do not collide. Clamp the full assembly together without glue and verify a 450 mm seat height, 740 mm writing height, and flat floor contact.
tools_used: Pocket-hole jig, stepped bit, stop collar, and long driver bit
Tape measure, pencil, and combination square
steps.safety: Clamp the jig and stock before drilling. Wear eye protection and keep fingers clear of the bit and screw exits.
steps.tip: Do not substitute ordinary countersunk screws for washer-head pocket screws.

steps.title: Sand and prefinish accessible faces
steps.text: Sand all parts with 120-grit followed by 180-grit, and gently ease exposed edges. Mask every glue-contact strip, then prime and apply two coats of red or black enamel as specified in the part notes. Apply three thin clear coats to both faces of P7, leaving its underside glue strips bare; allow approximately 2–4 hours between water-based coats and at least 24 hours before handling, or follow the product label if longer.
steps.safety: Control sanding dust with extraction and a respirator. Ventilate the finishing area and follow coating-label handling and disposal instructions.
steps.tip: Bare, clean wood must remain at every glued joint; glue will not reliably bond through paint.

steps.title: Join the seat to both supports
steps.text: Clamp P3 (seat) between P1 (right structural side) and P2 (left seat support), with its underside at 432 mm and front edge at z = 300 mm. Glue both seat edges and drive four 32 mm pocket screws per side from underneath P3 into the supports, eight screws total. Keep the supports square and clamp for at least 45 minutes, or longer if required by the glue label.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil, and combination square
steps.safety: Support the tall right panel against tipping and use a helper when repositioning it. Wear eye protection while driving screws.
steps.tip: Use a low clutch setting and stop when each washer head seats firmly.

steps.title: Install the back and rear brace
steps.text: Position P4 (back and rear brace) between the supports with its bottom at 350 mm and rear face flush at z = 740 mm. Glue its contacting side edges and the rear edge of P3, then drive five 32 mm pocket screws into P1 and two into P2 from P4's rear face. Drive four more 32 mm pocket screws from beneath P3 into P4, for eleven screws in this step. Clamp square for at least 45 minutes and leave the chair body supported while the glue develops strength.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil, and combination square
steps.safety: Use a helper to steady the assembly and wear eye protection. Keep the rear face unobstructed until all back screws are installed.
steps.tip: The upper back projects above P1; do not mistakenly align their top edges.

steps.title: Assemble the desk leg and apron
steps.text: Lay P5 (front desk leg) and P6 (front desk apron) on a padded bench with their top edges flush. Glue the apron end against the right side of the leg and drive three 32 mm pocket screws from the rear face of P6 into P5. Keep their front faces flush and clamp for at least 45 minutes.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil, and combination square
steps.safety: Clamp the subassembly before driving and wear eye protection.
steps.tip: The apron bottom is 180 mm below the leg top, not flush with the leg bottom.

steps.title: Connect the front desk frame
steps.text: Stand the chair body and position the P5/P6 subassembly with its front face aligned to P1's front edge. Glue P6's free end to P1 and drive three 32 mm pocket screws from the rear face of P6 into P1. Verify that P5 and P1 both finish at height 722 mm and that the unit rests flat, then clamp for at least 45 minutes.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil, and combination square
steps.safety: Have a helper stabilize the assembly until this joint is secured. Wear eye protection when driving screws.
steps.tip: Install these screws before the writing surface restricts access.

steps.title: Attach the writing surface
steps.text: With a helper, place P7 (writing surface) face down on padding and invert the supported assembly onto it, aligning all specified coordinates. Glue the contacting top edges of P1 and P6 and the top of P5. Drive three 32 mm pocket screws from P1, three from P6, and one from P5 into P7's underside, seven screws total. Clamp the contacts snugly for at least 45 minutes, and allow at least 24 hours of glue curing before placing weight on the unit.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil, and combination square
steps.safety: This assembly is awkward and heavy; use two people and stable blocking so the projecting back is not carrying the inverted unit. Wear eye protection while driving.
steps.tip: Keep the rear-left opening over the seat; the right writing wing extends 100 mm beyond P1.

steps.title: Touch up and inspect before use
steps.text: Return the unit upright with a helper, remove glue residue, and touch up the finishes without painting over loose or questionable joints. Allow the coatings to reach their labeled full-use cure, commonly 7 days, before regular seating. On a level floor, check for rocking, joint opening, sharp edges, and flex using progressively applied non-person ballast before a cautious seated trial; stop if anything moves or cracks. This low, broad unit is not intended to require a wall anti-tip tether, but its 820 mm back means tipping must still be assessed, and no one should climb, lean far backward, or sit on the writing surface.
tools_used: Tape measure, pencil, and combination square
steps.safety: Keep people clear during initial ballast checks and do not treat a home test as a certified load rating. Ventilate during finish touch-ups and use two people for lifting.
steps.tip: Reinspect the pocket-screw joints after the first week of use and periodically afterward; remove the unit from service if joints loosen.

safety_overview: Wear eye and hearing protection for cutting and drilling; use dust extraction and a particulate respirator when cutting or sanding plywood.
Clamp stock securely and support full sheets and offcuts so they cannot pinch a blade or fall.
Use sound furniture-grade plywood and correct pocket screws; reject delaminated panels, stripped holes, or split leg stock.
Use two people to turn and move the assembled unit, especially while the back projects beyond the supports.
Ventilate during finishing and wait for both glue and coatings to cure before use.
This is seating, not a step stool: do not climb on it, sit on the writing surface, or lean backward. Assess tipping before use and supervise children.

review.summary: The assembly sequence is workable, pocket-screw locations remain accessible, and the glued plywood panels provide substantial bracing. Prefinishing, glue-contact masking, inversion support, and initial safety checks are addressed. One minor hardware clarification is recommended.

issues.problem: J6 specifies coarse-thread pocket screws into an unspecified hardwood leg. Coarse threads can split dense hardwood or require excessive driving torque; the appropriate thread depends on the hardwood selected.
issues.fix: Specify the P5 hardwood species and follow the pocket-screw manufacturer's thread recommendation. For dense hardwood such as maple or oak, specify 32 mm fine-thread washer-head pocket screws for J6 and test the connection on matching scraps in step 3. Retain coarse-thread screws for joints whose receiving material is plywood, including J10.

plan.title: Round Side Table with Four Splayed Legs
plan.summary: A 600 mm diameter, 550 mm high side table matching the reference's round top, tapered legs and small underside cleat. A plywood top and purchased tapered legs keep the build practical. Angled mounting plates provide the structural leg connections. Intended for lamps, drinks and similar light household use, not sitting or standing.
assumptions: The reference depicts a light-duty side table, not a stool. The proposed service load is 15 kg distributed over the top; this is a design assumption, not a certified load rating.
The top is 25 mm birch plywood rather than solid wood, avoiding seasonal-movement problems at the leg plates.
The legs splay radially outward at 10 degrees. This is approximately 7 degrees when viewed from either the front or side, matching the reference.

Use four matching 10-degree mounting kits whose installed leg-shoulder stand-off is 3 mm. Confirm this dimension before cutting the legs; different hardware requires recalculating their finished length.

Purchased tapered legs are shortened from approximately 559 mm. Their finished diameter is approximately 44 mm at the upper shoulder and 26 mm at the foot; this is slightly heavier than the reference.

Calculated leg centerline lengths and coordinates retain decimals for drawing accuracy. Workshop layout uses a 522 mm vertical shoulder-to-floor jig and whole-millimeter measurements rather than attempting to measure four-decimal-place lengths.
Hardware is represented by joints rather than separate wooden-part geometry. The 3 mm gap above each leg is occupied by its mounting plate.
The reference's central rounded cleat is retained, although the plywood top does not require it for stiffness.
clarifying_questions: Is this strictly a light-duty side table, or must it support a person or a heavier specified load?

parts.name: Round top
parts.notes: Cut from a minimum 620 x 620 blank. Keep the plywood edge visible and clear-finish it, or paint the complete table.

parts.name: Purchased tapered legs, shortened and level-cut
parts.buy_spec: 22 inch unfinished tapered round wooden furniture leg, approximately 44 mm top diameter and 25 mm foot diameter, removable M8 hanger bolt; four matching legs compatible with 10-degree mounting plates
parts.notes: Finished centerline length is 522/cos(10 degrees), approximately 530 mm. Both wooden end faces must be parallel to the floor when mounted. Remove the hanger bolt before cutting the upper shoulder, then reinstall according to its manufacturer's instructions. Orient the two parallel cuts in the leg's radial splay plane. Actual purchased taper may vary slightly; select a matching set. Do not custom-turn these legs.

parts.name: Rounded underside cleat
parts.notes: Capsule-shaped plan outline with R20 ends. Grain runs along the 280 mm length. Three recessed screw seats permit sufficient screw penetration into the top.

joints.drive_from: From the exposed underside of P3 into the underside of P1, with the top upside down before installing the legs.
joints.note: Glue the mating faces. Locate screws 40, 140 and 240 mm from the cleat's left end on its width centerline. Counterbore each screw seat 10 mm deep, leaving 12 mm of cleat beneath the head; a 32 mm screw then penetrates the top by 20 mm and stops 5 mm short of its visible face. Use a depth stop.

fasteners.name: Made-to-drawing level-shoulder splayed-leg mounting kit
fasteners.size: 10-degree M8 connection; horizontal full-shoulder bearing flange; 3 mm installed shoulder-center stand-off; recessed threaded socket; compatible hanger bolt and locking mechanism; four included 20 mm mounting screws

joints.drive_from: From below through the mounting flange into the upside-down P1; thread each P2 into its socket and operate the supplier-specified accessible locking mechanism.
joints.note: The fixed P2 geometry has a floor-parallel upper shoulder, so conventional angled plates are incompatible. This joint requires a hardware supplier to furnish an expressly engineered kit for that shoulder geometry, not an assumed off-the-shelf substitute. Its horizontal bearing surface must support the entire approximately 44 mm shoulder, its threaded axis must incline 10 degrees radially outward, and its actual shoulder-center stand-off must be 3 mm. Specify a recessed socket providing at least 12 mm of usable M8 thread engagement while leaving at least 3 mm of plywood beneath the visible top face; the supplier must approve socket dimensions, mounting-screw pattern, hanger-bolt wood engagement after shoulder trimming, tightening torque and positive rotational locking. Four included 20 mm mounting screws must each penetrate the plywood by at least 12 mm without approaching the visible face closer than 3 mm. Require written suitability for a 15 kg distributed table load and foreseeable lateral handling loads, using these legs and 25 mm plywood. No glue; all locking components and mounting screws must be included in the kit. Do not purchase, cut or assemble against a generic angled-plate description. If a supplier cannot provide this kit and its installation drawing, stop: conventional hardware would require changing the fixed parts or geometry.

tools.alternative: Use the finish manufacturer's recommended applicator.

steps.title: Obtain compatible hardware before cutting
steps.text: The fixed P2 (purchased tapered leg) geometry requires level upper shoulders, which conventional angled leg plates do not support correctly. Obtain four made-to-drawing level-shoulder splayed-leg mounting kits meeting J2, with a supplier-approved installation drawing identifying the actual kit, full shoulder bearing, 10-degree threaded axis, measured 3 mm stand-off, bolt engagement, tightening torque and locking method. Have the supplier confirm suitability for the specified plywood, modified legs, 15 kg distributed load and lateral handling loads; no particular commercially available kit has been verified here. Trial-fit the actual hardware and an uncut leg in a scrap fixture, and make a layout jig showing the required 522 mm vertical shoulder-center-to-floor drop. If these requirements cannot be met, stop rather than substitute a conventional angled plate or change the fixed geometry.
tools_used: Adjustable bevel gauge or digital angle gauge
Drill and driver with pilot bits
steps.safety: Clamp the scrap fixture and wear eye protection when drilling. Obtain specialist hardware approval before making irreversible cuts.
steps.tip: The specified custom hardware is a prerequisite, not a claim that an ordinary angled mounting plate will work.

steps.title: Cut the circular top and rounded cleat
steps.text: Mark a 600 mm circle on P1 (round top) using a 300 mm radius. Cut just outside the line and sand back to it, keeping the edge square. Cut P3 (rounded underside cleat) to 280 x 40 x 22 mm and round each end to a 20 mm radius. A woodworking supplier can make these cuts instead of using a jigsaw.
steps.safety: Wear eye and hearing protection and a suitable dust mask. Support the blank securely, keep the blade clear of the bench, and unplug the saw before changing blades.
steps.tip: Do not cut the legs until the actual mounting kit has passed step 1.

steps.title: Prepare the shoulders and mark the feet using the actual hardware
steps.text: Only after step 1 is satisfied, remove each P2 hanger bolt and make its level upper-shoulder cut in a secured cradle, following the hardware supplier's approved shoulder drawing. Reinstall the kit's compatible hanger bolt with the supplier's specified wood engagement and projection; do not reuse an assumed pre-cut setting. On a scrap fixture, fully seat and positively lock each leg in its actual kit, confirm full shoulder contact, and label each leg, plate and rotational orientation. Use the height jig to mark its floor-parallel foot cut at a 522 mm vertical drop from the shoulder center, then remove the leg and cut the foot in the secured cradle. Check the approximately 530 mm finished centerline length in the jig and verify that both bearing faces are parallel when the leg is mounted.
tools_used: Miter saw with a secure round-stock cradle
Adjustable bevel gauge or digital angle gauge
steps.safety: Never hold round stock freehand against a powered saw fence. Clamp it in a cradle, keep hands outside the blade zone, and wear eye and hearing protection; have a woodworking shop make these cuts if secure workholding is unavailable.
steps.tip: A fine-tooth handsaw with a clamped angle guide is an alternative. Do not compensate for poor shoulder contact by tightening harder.

steps.title: Drill the cleat screw seats
steps.text: Mark three holes on P3's width centerline, 40, 140 and 240 mm from its left end. Drill a flat-bottomed recess at each mark to place the screw's bearing seat 10 mm below the underside, then drill a clearance hole through the remaining 12 mm. Dry-fit P3 centered under P1 at x = 160 mm and z = 280 mm, and transfer the pilot-hole locations.
tools_used: Drill and driver with pilot bits
Forstner or counterbore bit and drilling depth stop
steps.safety: Clamp the cleat before drilling and wear eye protection. Use a depth stop so the counterbore cannot break through.
steps.tip: Make a test screw seat in scrap to verify that the screw head bears properly and the driver fits inside the recess.

steps.title: Prepare the hardware recesses and sand
steps.text: Mark P1's four shoulder-center locations at x,z coordinates (190,190), (410,190), (190,410) and (410,410) mm, with each leg splaying toward its nearest bounding-square corner. Using the actual kits and their approved templates, prepare the recessed-socket pockets and mounting pilots, retaining at least 3 mm of plywood beneath the visible face and the specified screw penetration. Sand P1, P2 and P3 through 120 and 180 grit and lightly ease exposed edges without changing the leg bearing faces. Remove dust and preserve the matching hardware labels, orientation marks and bare cleat-gluing surfaces.
tools_used: Drill and driver with pilot bits
Forstner or counterbore bit and drilling depth stop
steps.safety: Clamp P1, wear eye protection and use positive drilling depth stops. Wear respiratory protection for sanding dust; have the supplier machine any pocket that cannot be made safely with these tools.
steps.tip: Use the supplier's socket template, not the apparent center of the flange, to position the shoulder accurately.

steps.title: Glue and screw the underside cleat
steps.text: Lay P1 upside down on padding and drill its three cleat pilot holes to a maximum depth of 20 mm. Apply a thin coat of glue to P3's mating face, position it centrally, and install three Wood screws #8 x 32mm from the recessed underside of P3 into P1. Clamp for at least 45 minutes, wipe away squeeze-out, and leave the assembly undisturbed overnight or as directed by the glue manufacturer.
tools_used: Drill and driver with pilot bits
Forstner or counterbore bit and drilling depth stop
steps.safety: Wear eye protection while drilling and use a positive depth stop to prevent breaking through the visible tabletop.
steps.tip: Stop tightening as soon as the joint closes; crushing the recessed screw seats weakens the cleat.

steps.title: Apply the clear finish
steps.text: Apply three thin coats of water-based furniture finish to P1, P2 and P3, including the tabletop underside and plywood edge. Keep threads, hardware pockets, flange seating areas and leg bearing faces free of finish buildup. Allow approximately 2–4 hours between coats, lightly sand with 220 grit where the product permits, and allow at least 24 hours before handling or the manufacturer's longer specified time.
steps.safety: Provide ventilation, wear the finish manufacturer's recommended gloves and eye protection, and keep containers away from children and ignition sources.
steps.tip: Full finish cure commonly takes several days; dry to the touch does not mean ready for wet cups.

steps.title: Install the approved kits and lock the legs
steps.text: With P1 upside down, seat the four made-to-drawing level-shoulder splayed-leg mounting kits in their prepared recesses and install four included 20 mm mounting screws per kit, driven from below into P1; use no glue. Fit each matching P2 leg at its labeled location and orientation, achieving the supplier-specified wood-thread and M8 socket engagement without the bolt bottoming out. Tighten to the supplied torque specification and engage the kit's positive locking mechanism while it remains accessible from below. Verify full upper-shoulder bearing, the 3 mm shoulder-center stand-off, outward 10-degree splay and correctly oriented level foot on every leg.
tools_used: Drill and driver with pilot bits
Adjustable bevel gauge or digital angle gauge
steps.safety: Support the top securely on padding. Do not put the table into service if any shoulder bears on only an edge, a bolt bottoms out, or a leg cannot be positively locked.
steps.tip: Do not back a leg off to align its foot; restore its trial-fitted, fully seated and locked orientation.

steps.title: Check height, stability and readiness
steps.text: Turn the table upright on a known flat surface and check for a 550 mm overall height and four firmly seated feet. If there is a slight rock, identify the high foot and hand-sand only its bearing face while retaining the level-cut angle. Check all mounting screws and leg locks, then apply a light distributed test load before normal use; this check does not replace the hardware supplier's approval. Observe the finish's full cure time and keep the table for light-duty use only, with no more than the specified 15 kg distributed service load.
steps.safety: Lift by the top with both hands rather than dragging the splayed legs. Never sit or stand on the table, and stop using it if any leg connection loosens.
steps.tip: Check stability on a flat board before altering a leg; an uneven floor can imitate a cutting error.

safety_overview: Wear eye protection for cutting and drilling, hearing protection around power saws, and respiratory protection for wood dust.
Clamp round legs in a proper cradle before cutting; never attempt unsupported round-stock cuts.
Use drilling depth stops to prevent screws and drill bits from piercing the tabletop.
Use matched, load-appropriate angled leg kits and follow their installation and locking instructions.
Ventilate during finishing and observe the product's handling and full-cure times.
This is light-duty furniture, not seating or a step stool; do not climb, stand or sit on it.

hardware.name: Made-to-drawing level-shoulder splayed-leg mounting kit
hardware.size: 10-degree M8 connection; horizontal full-shoulder bearing flange; 3 mm installed shoulder-center stand-off; recessed threaded socket; compatible hanger bolt and locking mechanism; four included 20 mm mounting screws

review.summary: The assembly sequence and tool access are generally practical, but the prescribed upper leg cuts are not established as compatible with the angled mounting hardware. Resolve that connection before buying hardware or trimming the legs.

issues.problem: Step 3 requires cutting each leg's upper shoulder parallel to the floor. Typical angled mounting plates instead accept a shoulder perpendicular to the leg and hanger-bolt axis. A floor-parallel shoulder can bear on only one edge of the angled plate, preventing firm seating and allowing the connection to loosen under sideways loads. The unspecified mounting kit does not establish compatibility with this modified shoulder. Cutting the shoulder also changes the hanger bolt's available engagement.
issues.fix: Select and identify the actual mounting kit before cutting P2, and follow its specified shoulder shape, bolt engagement and locking method. For a conventional angled plate, retain the purchased upper shoulder and hanger-bolt installation and shorten the leg only at its foot. Trial-install and fully tighten or lock each leg, label its position and rotational orientation, then mark the floor-parallel foot cut. Remove the legs and make those cuts in the secured cradle. Update P2, steps 1 and 3, and J2 to use the selected kit's actual installed stand-off rather than requiring an unverified 3 mm value. If retaining the beveled upper shoulder, specify hardware expressly designed to support it.
